title: Measuring Validator and Sandboxed-Execution Coverage for LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts: A Paired Confirmatory Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) measuring the marginal detection benefit of automated sandboxed emulation over a strong deterministic validator for LLM-generated intent→configuration artifacts. Using the declared model (gpt-5-mini) under shared_initial_candidate semantics, we evaluated Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) detected 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) detected 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting records model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call). These artifact-grounded results fall far below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We report the preregistered design, exact quantitative outcomes, run accounting diagnostics, an explanation for the negligible guarded benefit in this regime, and concise reproducibility pointers into the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models are increasingly proposed as intent→configuration and AIOps co-pilots in NetOps workflows. Operational trustworthiness for such agentic pipelines depends largely on surrounding deterministic validators, verifiers, and sandboxed execution to detect and mitigate incorrect or unsafe outputs [1], [2]. Prior work documents generate→validate→repair patterns and prototype runtime emulation; however, quantitative, cross-vendor estimates of the marginal value added by sandboxed emulation over strong static validators are scarce. We therefore preregistered a confirmatory paired experiment to answer the primary research question: For synthetic intent→configuration tasks, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same deterministic validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation? Our contribution is an artifact-grounded measurement under strict preregistration examining that marginal detection effect, exact run accounting, and a focused analysis of why a guarded stage may produce little aggregate benefit when paired with a high-coverage validator.
sections.related_work: Prior surveys and system reports emphasize workflow-centred mitigations—static validators, formal verification tools, and sandboxed execution—to reduce NetOps operational risk [1], [2]. Prototype tools and program-verification transfers indicate that emulation or formal analysis can expose runtime failures missed by static checks in specific settings [3]; LLM-assisted code and configuration work also shows that external verifiers improve correctness in many cases [4]. These bodies of work motivate measuring guarded-stage marginal effects rather than producing another model leaderboard: our study reports a preregistered paired estimate and situates it within validator-coverage and task-bank construction considerations. The present study is narrower in scope than broad surveys but complements them by providing a tightly controlled, preregistered, artifact-archived measurement of validator versus guarded detection coverage.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and main design. We froze a machine-readable preregistration (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) before execution. Design: paired-binary with shared_initial_candidate semantics (one sampled initial candidate produced per task and reused by both baseline and guarded pipelines). This design ensures any between-condition discordance can arise only from (i) guarded-stage emulation observations that reveal a violation not encoded in the static validator, or (ii) a permitted downstream repair-stage invocation recorded in the execution manifest. Planned confirmatory Npairs = 720.

Task bank and inclusion rules. Confirmatory items were synthetic intent→configuration tasks from the intent_configuration_repair_v1 family spanning three abstracted vendor-CLI families and three topology templates (leaf-spine, 3-node service chain, triangle). Inclusion required vendor-specific parser acceptance (up to two deterministic reseeds on parser failure per the missingness plan). No irrecoverable parser exclusions occurred in the confirmatory set (complete_pair_count = 720). Representative task manifests and per-episode payloads (e.g., required_sequence, intent, initial/expected final state) are archived in the execution bundle.

Model and sampling semantics. The declared/requested model was "gpt-5-mini" (provider entry: openai_responses) and the archived execution/model_configuration.json records max_output_tokens = 2000 and temperature = null. Explicit clarification: temperature = null indicates the request did not supply an explicit temperature parameter; null does not imply deterministic sampling (temperature=0) nor guarantee identical outputs across provider calls. The preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced: the same sampled candidate per pair was used for both baseline and guarded analyses and is recorded in per-episode archives; therefore, any between-condition difference is attributable only to guarded-stage dynamics (emulation observation or the permitted repair-stage invocation).

Validator and guarded pipeline. Baseline: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 performing full intent-constraint checks (syntax, workflow ordering, required-field presence, and policy-level constraints). Guarded: baseline validator followed by an automated sandboxed emulation harness that executes the candidate against the emulated topology and reports runtime observations beyond static checks. The repair policy allowed at most one repair-stage model call per task. All validator and emulation traces and scoring outputs are archived.

Statistical analysis and preregistered estimands. The primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. The preregistered primary analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1 (McNemar-style exact test and a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI). Power planning targeted a minimum effect-of-interest of 0.20 (20 percentage points) with α = 0.05 and ≈80% power under conservative baseline assumptions; sensitivity analyses and preregistered multiplicity corrections for secondary exploratory comparisons were specified in the preregistration. The primary analysis used the complete-pair policy (exclude irrecoverable technical failures) as preregistered.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory outcome (complete paired set, Npairs = 720). Analysis artifacts show: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (detected by guarded only), n01 = 0 (detected by baseline only), n00 = 0 (detected by neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. These numbers are reproduced verbatim from the archived paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor outputs and associated CSV artifacts (analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv).

Run accounting and discordant-pair attribution. The authoritative execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json; summarized in the archived manifest) records model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call) and stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 720, repair = 1. Because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, the sole mechanisms for the single n10 discordance are (i) a guarded-stage emulation observation not encoded as a static validator violation, or (ii) the recorded single repair-stage invocation. The single discordant episode is recorded in execution/raw_results.jsonl; its canonical file SHA-256 (as archived) is df367ecc40a6f0eaf402129260e11d8450884a4ea5fdb94a602e0d2513aef0e8. Independent verifiers can locate the discordant pair by opening execution/raw_results.jsonl (archive) and searching for the single record with baseline_score = 0 and guarded_score = 1; that record contains the pair_id and per-episode validator and emulation traces linking the discordance to the unique repair-stage invocation. The deterministic reconciliation artifact analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json corroborates the single repair-stage invocation in provider_call_audit and the contingency accounting (n11=719, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0).

Representative per-episode diagnostics. Representative archived per-episode validator traces show validator_id = deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and validator_version = 5.0. The representative examples included in the archive (task-000001 through task-000006) illustrate typical intent→configuration mappings, normalized candidate text, and validator before/after states (validation_before and validation_after structures). These representative records show that most sampled candidates matched the validator's rule set (violation_count = 0 in most episodes), producing a strong baseline ceiling effect. The single discordant episode's per-episode trace (found as above in execution/raw_results.jsonl) contains validator_trace and emulation observation fields and the repair_provider_trace when a repair-stage call occurred; those per-episode fields explain why the guarded pipeline produced the lone additional detection.

Missingness and preregistration compliance. The preregistered missingness plan (deterministic reseeds up to two times, deterministic replacements if irrecoverable) was followed. The analysis/missingness_summary.csv reports complete_pairs = 720 and zero parser/infrastructure-driven exclusions. No deviations from the preregistration affecting the primary estimand were recorded in the archived deviation log. All analysis artifacts referenced here are included in the execution bundle and reconcile deterministically as shown in the archived reconciliation artifact.
sections.discussion:
Why was the guarded-stage aggregated benefit negligible? The archived evidence supports three artifact-grounded explanatory factors. First, validator ceiling effect: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 provided near-universal coverage for the curated syntactic and explicit semantic misconfigurations encoded in the synthetic task bank (baseline success rate = 0.9986). Second, task curation: confirmatory tasks were parser-validated synthetic items designed to exercise workflow policies but not adversarially crafted to evade the validator; this concentrates items within the validator's coverage envelope. Third, shared_initial_candidate semantics and run accounting: identical initial candidates across conditions constrain discordance to downstream guarded-stage outputs and the single permitted repair invocation, which the provider-call audit records.

Operational implications and boundary conditions. Our finding implies that when a high-coverage static validator exists and inputs conform to that validator's expected patterns, guarded sandboxed emulation may add negligible marginal detection value at the aggregate level. This conditional interpretation must not be overgeneralized: in operational regimes with noisy natural-language intents, adversarial mutations, stateful multi-step interactions, or validator gaps (different vendor behaviors), guarded runtime checks and higher-fidelity emulation can yield substantive added value. The archived per-episode traces illustrate many cases where emulation and static checks agree and point to the necessity of constructing adversarial and broader cross-vendor task banks to stress guarded stages.

Statistical interpretation and design sensitivity. The study was preregistered and powered for a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20. The observed discordant counts (n10 = 1) produce an upper 95% CI bound ≈0.00417, demonstrating the realized aggregated effect is orders of magnitude below the preregistered minimum effect-of-interest. Thus this is a narrowly scoped near-zero finding relative to our original design sensitivity; it should not be taken as evidence that guarded stages are universally unnecessary. Instead, it quantifies a regime—synthetic, parser-validated tasks with a strong static validator—where the guarded-stage marginal benefit is negligible.

Threats to validity and recommended follow-ups. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics isolate guarded-stage contributions but remove generation variability between conditions; provider-side nondeterminism remains a residual uncertainty despite deterministic reconciliation. Construct validity: our binary detection scoring reflects intent-constraint checks and emulation-observed violations but does not directly measure downstream operational impact (user downtime, rollback cost). External validity: single declared model family (gpt-5-mini), single validator implementation, and synthetic parser-validated tasks limit generalizability. Conclusion validity: the study targeted a 0.20 effect; observed effect is far smaller and secondary per-class/vendor estimates remain exploratory. We recommend targeted follow-up experiments using adversarial task generation, multiple independent validator families, and higher-fidelity stateful emulators; those follow-ups are feasible using the archived experiment harness and per-episode artifact formats.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a strong deterministic validator with the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on synthetic LLM-generated NetOps tasks. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting shows one repair-stage invocation corresponding to the single guarded-only detection; because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, archived per-episode traces permit independent verification of that mapping in execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 df367ecc40a6f0eaf402129260e11d8450884a4ea5fdb94a602e0d2513aef0e8). We interpret the result as arising from validator ceiling effects and curated task design and recommend follow-up work on adversarial and multi-vendor task banks, multiple validator families, and higher-fidelity emulation to identify regimes where guarded stages provide substantive added value.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and create a ceiling effect for a strong validator; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validator families.

Preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across paired conditions) isolate guarded-stage contribution but remove between-condition generation variability; this design choice constrains discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and large-scale stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could change outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that design sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime rather than a general negative result for all NetOps workflows.

Provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching remain residual uncertainties despite deterministic reconciliation procedures; these are discussed in the execution manifest and provider_call_audit artifacts.
